title: Sound, Heat & Light
subtitle: Three kinds of energy, three ways of travelling.
objectives: Explain how sound travels and why it needs a medium
Name the three ways heat moves
Describe light as something that travels in straight lines until it meets something
Compare the speeds of sound and light

cards.title: Three energies you meet every second
cards.text: Sound needs something to travel through. Heat has three routes. Light goes straight until something stops it. Different rules each.

cards.title: A squeeze passed along
cards.text: Sound is a vibration passed from particle to particle. No particles, no sound.
points: **Air particles bump** into their neighbours and pass the shake along.
**In space there is nothing to bump.** Silence, genuinely.
**Solids carry it faster** than air, because the particles are closer.
**Your eardrum** is just a surface being pushed and pulled.

cards.title: You can see the vibration
cards.alt: Rice grains caught bouncing in the air above a drum head as it is struck
cards.text: The grains are in the air. The skin is pushing them, and pushing the air the same way.

cards.title: Pump the air out
cards.text: A bell in a jar. One of the two waves stops working.

cards.title: What a fan's noise is actually telling you
cards.text: A fan makes several sounds at once, and each one has a different source inside the case.
points: **The whoosh** is blades chopping air. Normal, rises with speed.
**A hum** is the motor's magnetic field vibrating the metal.
**A rattle or grind** is bearings, and that one is a fault.
**Listening is diagnosis.** You are hearing parts, not just noise.

question.text: Sound travels faster in air than in steel.
question.explain: Solids carry sound faster because their particles sit closer together and pass the vibration on sooner.

cards.title: Three routes, not one
cards.text: Heat always moves from hotter to colder. How it gets there is what you have to name.
points: **Conduction**: through a solid, particle to particle.
**Convection**: a fluid carries it, hot rising and cold sinking.
**Radiation**: straight through space, no material needed.
**The Sun reaches you by radiation.** Nothing else could cross the gap.

question.text: How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?
question.explain: Space is nearly empty, so there is nothing to conduct through or carry it. Only radiation crosses.

cards.title: A fan does not cool the room. It cools you
cards.text: Check the thermometer. A fan running in a closed room makes it very slightly warmer.
points: **The motor turns electricity into heat** as well as movement.
**You feel cooler** because moving air speeds up sweat evaporating.
**Evaporation takes heat** off your skin with it.
**Leaving a fan on in an empty room** warms it and cools nobody.

cards.title: Straight lines, until something interferes
cards.text: Light travels in straight lines. Everything you see is light that bounced off something into your eye.
points: **Reflection**: it bounces off.
**Refraction**: it bends on entering a new material.
**Absorption**: it is taken in and becomes heat.
**Shadows are proof** that it does not bend round corners.

cards.title: White was never one colour
cards.alt: A glass prism splitting a narrow white beam into a fanned spectrum of colours
cards.text: The glass bends each colour by a different amount, so they come out separated.

cards.title: Film explosions in space should be silent
cards.text: You would see the flash. You would hear absolutely nothing, however close you were.
points: **No air means no particles** to carry the vibration.
**Astronauts talk by radio**, which is a light-type wave, not sound.
**Touch helmets together** and you would hear through the solid.
**Films add sound anyway.** Silence does not sell tickets.

question.text: Why do you see a shadow behind a solid object?
options: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend round it
question.explain: No light reaches that patch because nothing bent it round the obstacle.

cards.title: Counting the gap to a lightning strike
cards.text: You see the flash immediately and hear the thunder later. The gap is a measurement.
points: **Light travels about 300,000 km every second.** Effectively instant.
**Sound manages about 340 metres a second.**
**Three seconds of gap** is roughly one kilometre away.
**No gap at all** means it is on top of you.

terms.def: Heat passing through a solid, particle to particle.
Heat carried by a moving fluid, hot rising and cold sinking.
Heat travelling as waves, needing no material.
Light bending as it enters a different material.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Sound needs particles. Space is silent.
Heat moves by conduction, convection or radiation.
Light goes straight; shadows prove it.
Light is effectively instant, sound is about 340 m/s.

quiz.text: Why is there no sound in space?
options: There are almost no particles to pass the vibration on
quiz.explain: Sound is a vibration handed between particles. Remove the particles and nothing carries it.
quiz.objective: Explain how sound travels and why it needs a medium

quiz.explain: Particles are closest together in a solid, so the vibration passes on soonest.
quiz.objective: Explain how sound travels and why it needs a medium

quiz.text: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth by…
quiz.explain: Space is nearly empty, so only radiation can cross it.
quiz.objective: Name the three ways heat moves

quiz.text: Hot air rising above a radiator is an example of…
quiz.explain: A moving fluid carrying heat is convection.
quiz.objective: Name the three ways heat moves

quiz.text: A metal spoon getting hot in soup is…
quiz.explain: Heat passes through the solid metal from particle to particle.
quiz.objective: Name the three ways heat moves

quiz.text: An electric fan lowers the temperature of a closed room.
quiz.explain: The motor adds a little heat. It cools people by speeding up evaporation, not the room.
quiz.objective: Name the three ways heat moves

quiz.explain: Nothing bends it round the obstacle, so that patch gets no light.
quiz.objective: Describe light as something that travels in straight lines until it meets something

quiz.text: Light bending as it passes into water is called…
quiz.objective: Describe light as something that travels in straight lines until it meets something

quiz.text: You see lightning three seconds before the thunder. Roughly how far away is it?
quiz.explain: Sound covers about 340 m each second, so three seconds is close to a kilometre.
quiz.objective: Compare the speeds of sound and light

quiz.text: Why do you see the flash before you hear the thunder?
options: Light is much faster than sound
quiz.explain: Light is effectively instant over that distance; sound takes about three seconds per kilometre.
quiz.objective: Compare the speeds of sound and light

quiz.text: A grinding noise from a fan most likely means…
quiz.explain: Whoosh is blades and hum is the motor, but a grind or rattle is a bearing fault.
quiz.objective: Explain how sound travels and why it needs a medium

quiz.text: Heat always moves from the hotter thing to the colder one.
quiz.explain: That direction is what heat transfer means. Only a pump, like a fridge, can appear to reverse it.
quiz.objective: Name the three ways heat moves

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 8 Science, three energy forms in one week, so each is given one clear rule rather than full coverage: sound needs a medium, heat has three named routes, light travels straight. The fan appears twice on purpose. Its noises are a diagnosis he can practise, and the fact that a fan warms a room while cooling a person is the week's best misconception-breaker, since it separates temperature from how something feels. The lightning gap gives him a number to use.
discussion: If a fan warms the room, why does it feel cooler?
What are the different noises inside a fan?
extension: Count the seconds between flash and thunder in the next storm.
Listen to a fan on each speed and name which noise changes.
misconceptions: That a fan cools a room.
That shadows are made of something.
